properties.name: OBSERVED 2026-09-28 (v0.74.0, read in code): collapse_decision moves a Decision to ACCEPTED, takes no approver parameter, and neither refuses nor reports the missing signature. It is the one settling path the 2026-09-06 "the owner's word in one call" sweep did not reach
properties.statement:
FOUND while mapping every path that settles intent for the exposed-server identity work (issue #616, dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id, settled the same day).

· reflow2-core alternatives.rs collapse_decision (about line 337): "the winner is chosen, the Decision moves to `accepted`, the losers are superseded".
· reflow2-mcp tools/exchange.rs collapse_decision (line 904): calls g.collapse_decision(decision_id, winner_id, note). It has no `approver` in its request, and no sign_as_approver.

Compare dec:idea-should-a-constructor-accept-the-owners-word-in-one-call (DECIDED): "a status past the landing default REFUSED without an approver ... the status setters take `approver` too and REPORT its absence". collapse_decision is a status setter in effect, and does neither. On reflow2's own design, CI's intent-authority gate would catch an accepted Decision with no approver edge (fact:an-accepted-status-written-without-its-approver-failed-the-intent-gate-in-ci). In a consumer's design, which runs no such gate, a collapsed decision reads as settled with nobody's name on it, against the ENFORCED rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word.

NOT ROOT-CAUSED; this is an observation. The measurement is by reading, not by a run. Other paths the same map found that settle without the typed approver door: acknowledge_gap and acknowledge_defect write an accepted Decision by design (their _by form names the judge); the generic create_node/create_nodes tools, import_graph and apply_merge write any status. The exposed-server work plans ONE choke point in the core (create_node / create_edge, under the write lock) that every settling write passes, which would cover all of these at once rather than one tool at a time.

2026-09-29, PARTLY RETIRED by reflow2 #628 (squash db305d4), and left open on purpose.

FIXED: collapse_decision now takes `approver` and `acted_at`, draws AUTHORED_BY role=approver on the Decision it accepts, and without one records the choice and says it carries nobody's name, like every other setter. It is also one of the nine tools that declare what settles them, in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/settles.rs, served as _meta["reflow2/settles"]. Pinned by crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/every_settling_call_declares_what_settles_it.rs, which was observed failing on origin/main 449ba2b (collapse_decision refused `approver` as an unknown field).

STILL TRUE, and not covered by #628: the generic writers (create_node, create_nodes, import_graph, apply_merge) still write any status without the typed approver door. The declaration covers the tools that take an approver, not the generic ones.

The branch's change record, chg:every-settling-call-declares-what-settles-it, is in main's committed export, not in this live store.

2026-09-30, CLOSED by reflow2 #635 (squash 3a14696). The generic writers this fact left open are now covered, all reading one settle table, reflow2_core::intent::SETTLING:
- create_node and create_nodes take `approver` (per item on create_nodes) and REFUSE an unsigned settle;
- import_graph, apply_merge and mirror_surface write it and NAME it under `settled_without_approver`;
- replace_text refuses an edit that would settle.
Pinned by crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/every_writer_settles_through_one_rule.rs, observed failing first on origin/main 6329079. It reads its writer list off the served surface, so a new door fails it. With #628's typed doors, no served writer now settles a status with nobody's name and says nothing.

The approver-ROLE half of the cure is NOT a status settle. It covers a forged AUTHORED_BY approver edge through create_edge(s), draw_edges, acknowledge_gaps items or import. It is still owed in R-S3 and tracked on fact:root-cause-the-settle-rule-guards-the-typed-doors-and-the-generic-writers-go-around-it-2026-09-29.
